source_book: The Brand Relationship Spectrum — Aaker & Joachimsthaler (2000)

test_cases.prompt: We want to brand everything under one master like Virgin does.
test_cases.expected_behavior: Activate aaker-relation-branded-house; run it as the DEFAULT and design the identity set.

test_cases.prompt: Leverage our strong master across all these offerings for clarity and synergy.
One master across countries, but GE Capital vs GE Appliances need different identities.
test_cases.expected_behavior: Activate aaker-relation-branded-house; apply the 'limited identities sharing common elements' nuance.

test_cases.prompt: We need a separate brand for each segment because the parent would clash.
test_cases.expected_behavior: Do NOT activate aaker-relation-branded-house; activate aaker-relation-house-of-brands (opposite end).

test_cases.prompt: Where on the spectrum should this new offering go?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Do NOT activate aaker-relation-branded-house; activate aaker-relation-select-separation (decision).

test_cases.prompt: Our master has weak equity in this category — is branded house still the default?
test_cases.expected_behavior: Activate aaker-relation-branded-house but note: default only holds when the master is strong/credible; if not, separation (house-of-brands/endorsed) may be warranted — hand to aaker-relation-select-separation.

notes: ≥3 should_trigger + 2 should_not_trigger (sibling baits: aaker-relation-house-of-brands, aaker-relation-select-separation) + 1 edge.
